previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and insulin-dependent diabetes was admitted for acute-on-chronic systolic heart failure exacerbated by dietary indiscretion. He presented with shortness of breath, orthopnea, bilateral leg edema, and chest tightness. Chest imaging showed moderate pulmonary edema, and labs revealed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine. He was treated with intravenous diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and optimized on heart failure medications including digoxin and losartan. His kidney function improved, and his volume status stabilized. Diabetes management was adjusted with increased insulin dosing, and pravastatin and benzonatate were added. He was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions on daily weights, low-salt diet, and close follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is ___ yo M with a PMH of HF (likely cocaine induced, 
last EF ___, HTN, DMII, HCV, COPD, schizophrenia, with 1 
week of worsening DOE and increased ankle edema, likely 
precipitated by cocaine use and ramen noodles. 

# Systolic HF exacerbation: Non-ischemic CM, likely cocaine 
related per prior notes. EF ___ in ___. The patient 
has been admitted multiple times in the past year for similar 
symptoms. His exacerbation is likely precipitated by dietary 
indiscretion and cocaine use. CXR suggestive of edema, pt with 
crackles, elevated JVP, and some peripheral edema. No evidence 
of infection. Low suspicion for coronary event with only 
slightly elevated Tn (in setting of ___ and ECG at baseline. Pt 
was treated with boluses of 160mg IV lasix, 5mg metolazone 
daily, and a lasix drip at 20mg/hr. Dyspnea and edema improved. 
The pt lost a total of 15 pounds and discharge weight was 179 
lbs. Pt remained hemodynamically stable throughout admission. 
Home losartan and digoxin continued. Pt is not on a home beta 
blocker due to concern over combining beta blocker and cocaine 
use. Pt instructed to avoid cocaine and salty foods.

# ___: Pt was also in ___ on admission, with creatinine 2.4, 
likely from poor forward flow, as it resolved w/ diuresis (pt's 
baseline had ranged 1.5-2.0). On day of discharge, creatinine 
was 1.8. During previous admissions as well, pt's creatinine has 
improved w/ diuresis.

# DMII: Very difficult to control on prior admissions w/ 
previous hospitalization complicated by hypoglycemia. Here, 
glucose ranged high 100s to 300s. A1c 9.4 on admission. Home 
insulin glargine 48 BID increased to 50 units bid. Pt also 
received ISS while here. He will require further insulin 
titration as outpatient.

# HTN: Blood pressure on admission very close to baseline 90-100 
systolic.  As above, home losartan continued.

# Hepatitis C: Positive VL in ___. No history of treatment. 
Outpatient antiviral therapy could be considered if pt able to 
comply with treatment.

# Substance abuse:  Pt encouraged not to use cocaine. Social 
work consulted. 

# Hyperlipidemia:  Continued pravastatin 40 mg daily  

# GERD:  Continued omeprazole  

# Anxiety:  Continued lorazepam PRN  

# Gout:  Continued colchine 0.6 mg daily  

Transitional Issues:
- Pt's glucose here was not well-controlled. He may need a 
higher dose of basal insulin. He is being discharged on 50 units 
lantus bid (in place of 48 units bid), and this may need to be 
uptitrated. A1c found to be 9.4.
- Discharge weight is 179 lbs (pt down 15 pounds during this 
admission)
- Pt should be encouraged to avoid cocaine and salty foods

FINDINGS: 

The cardiac, mediastinal and hilar contours appear unchanged.  The heart is
mild to moderately enlarged but unchanged.  Fissures are minimally thickened. 
There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  A diffuse moderate interstitial
abnormality appears very similar to the prior studies.  No superimposed acute
focal abnormality is identified.  There has been no definite change.

IMPRESSION: 

Similar moderate diffuse interstitial abnormality.  Findings could be seen
with recurring or persistent pulmonary edema, which seems mostly likely,
although an underlying interstitial abnormality could also be considered.
